strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-23503: scipy.stats.trapezoid.fit with no starting values falls back to the triangular edge c=d=1 and fails to converge. Build SciPy at the buggy commit ce2bbfebaa76, run the PR's test_trapezoid_fit_convergence_gh23503 (in test_distributions.py), and expect it to fail on the buggy build and pass once trapezoid_gen._fitstart supplies args (0.33, 0.66) when args is None. The version pins are unstated in the evidence, so they are chosen here and flagged.

system_packages: libopenblas-dev or the system BLAS/LAPACK used by the SciPy build
build_commands: git checkout ce2bbfebaa76 && git submodule update --init --recursive (if needed)
pip install -r requirements/build.txt (or the build-system requires in pyproject.toml at that commit)
pinned_because: numpy 1.26.4 and Python 3.12 come from the reporter's environment in issue #23503, not from any documented requirement; they are chosen to match the reporter, and the test's seeded RNG makes the transition independent of exact patch versions

The build dependencies must be those pinned at ce2bbfebaa76 (pyproject.toml / requirements/build.txt) because the in-repo meson build fails with mismatched Cython/pythran versions; this is an era-inferred constraint, not a documented one for the reproducer
scipy version is not pinned: the reproduction builds the buggy and fixed revisions from source, so the installed scipy 1.13.0 from the reporter is not used

strategy.test_command: python dev.py test -t scipy.stats.tests.test_distributions.py::TestTrapezoid::test_trapezoid_fit_convergence_gh23503 (if the class name differs, use: python -m pytest scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py -k trapezoid_fit_convergence_gh23503 -v); also run python dev.py test -t scipy.stats.tests.test_continuous_basic -k trapezoid and python dev.py test -t scipy.stats.tests.test_fit -k trapezoid to check the xfail-set changes
strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py::test_trapezoid_fit_convergence_gh23503 (added after test_trapezoid_vect in the trapezoid test class); it draws 1000 samples from trapezoid(0.3, 0.7, -1, 2) with rng default_rng(23842359234598263956), calls stats.trapezoid.fit(x) with no starting values, then asserts fitted c and d are not both within atol 0.1 of 1 and that nnlf(fitted) < nnlf(true)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision ce2bbfebaa76 the test fails: the unguided fit returns c and d near 1 (triangular), so np.allclose(fitted_c, 1, atol=0.1) or the d check is True and the 'not' assertion fails. On the fixed revision the test passes: _fitstart supplies (0.33, 0.66) for shapes, the fit moves off c=d=1, and the fitted nnlf is below the true-parameter nnlf. The transition is the test outcome only.
strategy.numerical_probe: Before running the test, check that trapezoid_gen._fitstart on the buggy build returns shapes (1, 1) when args is None, so the failure path is confirmed without relying on the printed fit values.

input_output_examples.input: scipy.stats.trapezoid.fit(rvs, floc=0, scale=1) with rvs = scipy.stats.trapezoid(0.3, 0.7, 0, 1).rvs(1000, random_state=42)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: fit does not converge; fitted c and d remain near 1.0 (triangular distribution)
input_output_examples.expected_output: fitted c and d not near (1.0, 1.0); the PR test asserts fitted values are not both within 0.01 of 1.0

risks: The PR test's tolerance is atol=0.1 on c and d and the llf comparison; the reproducer in the issue uses different parameters (0.3, 0.7, 0, 1 with random_state=42), so the reproducer and the PR test may not both trigger the bug on the same build

The evidence says the infrastructure ignores parameter guesses unless both are passed and never calls the function with args; if fit() never reaches the args-is-None branch, the fixed path may not be exercised and the fix may not change the test outcome
Stopping criterion, iteration count and optimizer tolerance are not stated, so a different platform or BLAS could shift the fitted values near the bound

Platform dependence is unknown: the evidence does not say whether the defect appears on all architectures, so it may not transition on a platform other than the reporter's, and a sanitiser build is not needed but was not ruled out

The test_continuous_basic and test_fit changes remove trapezoid from xfail sets; those sets are separate tests and may fail on the fixed revision if the fit now converges too slowly or to a poor optimum
Build dependency versions at ce2bbfebaa76 are not stated in the evidence; a mismatch can break the build before the test runs

oracle.tolerance: atol=0.1 on fitted c and d in the PR test; the reviewer's proposed assert_allclose tolerance is not stated
oracle.why: The PR test is property-based against the triangular point (c=d=1) with a stated absolute tolerance and an llf comparison, so the transition is decided by that tolerance and not by exact values

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The unguided fit returns c and d near 1, so np.allclose(fitted_c, 1, atol=0.1) is True and the 'assert not' fails with AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With _fitstart supplying (0.33, 0.66), c and d move off the triangular point, both 'not allclose' asserts hold, and fitted nnlf is below true nnlf, so the test passes.
